reply.text:
I'll check your deadlift history to see where you're at with this. Grip is the limiter on deadlifts for a lot of people, especially as the weight goes up. Straps work if your back is the actual limit — they let your grip take a step back so your back muscles do the work instead of your hands. But first: are you pulling conventional or sumo, and what weight are we talking about? The answer changes a little depending on how heavy you are relative to your strength.

The other side is grip work itself — it builds over weeks, same as anything else. If you want your grip to hold with the bar, dead hangs, farmer carries and rows all build it without needing to do much. But straps are legit if you're chasing a heavy pull and grip is the one thing stopping it.
